name: Turkic Khaganates (Göktürks)
summary: The first state to use the name “Türk” politically. Founded by Bumin in 552, its empire stretched from Manchuria to the Black Sea; it split in 603 and revived as the Second Turkic Khaganate (682–744).

location.value: The Mongolian Plateau and Central Asia, stretching from Manchuria to the Black Sea.

terrain.value: Steppe grasslands, mountains (Altai) and oases along the Silk Road.
terrain.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

climate.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

resources.value: Horses and herds; iron (the Göktürks were said to be ironworkers for the Rouran).
resources.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

disasters.value: Heavy snows and livestock losses weakened the Eastern khaganate before the Tang conquest.
disasters.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

urbanisation.value: Mostly nomadic; Suyab in the west was a trading town.
urbanisation.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

disease.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

migration.value: Turkic peoples later spread across Central Asia and into Anatolia.
migration.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

economicBase.value: Herding and taxing Silk Road trade.
economicBase.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

tradeRoutes.value: Controlled the Silk Road; Sogdian merchants carried silk to Persia and Byzantium.
tradeRoutes.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

moneyAndTax.value: Coins with Sogdian legends; tribute from China.

inequality.value: The Ashina royal clan ruled over subject tribes.
inequality.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

governmentType.value: A nomadic khaganate, with eastern and western wings under the khagan and the yabgu.

keyRulers.value: Bumin Qaghan (552), Istämi (552–575, west), Tardu (599–603); later Bilge Khagan and Kül Tegin (8th century).

succession.value: Disputes among the Ashina clan led to civil war (581) and the split (603).
succession.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

institutions.value: Titles such as khagan and yabgu; a nomadic court.
institutions.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

stability.value: Civil war from 581 and division in 603.

armyAndTech.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

majorWars.value: Wars with Sui and Tang China; Tang conquered the Eastern khaganate (630) and the Western (657).

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with Byzantium against Persia; rivals of Tang China and the Sasanians.
alliancesRivals.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

inventions.value: The Old Turkic script was invented in the first half of the 6th century.

scienceEducation.value: The Orkhon inscriptions (c. 732) are the oldest known texts in a Turkic language.
scienceEducation.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

openness.value: Used Sogdian for official texts and coins.

religion.value: Tengrism (worship of the sky god Tengri), and some Buddhism.

artsArchitecture.value: Stone memorial stelae and “balbal” stone figures.
artsArchitecture.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

socialStructure.value: Royal clan, nobles (beg), herders, subject tribes.
socialStructure.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

sharedIdentity.value: The first state to use the name “Türk” politically.

neighbours.value: China (Sui, Tang), Sasanian Persia, Byzantium, Rouran.
neighbours.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

ideasReligions.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

colonisation.source: Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

peakPeriod.value: About 557, from Manchuria to the Black Sea.

declineSignals.value: Civil war among the Ashina princes and military pressure from Sui and Tang China.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: First Turkic Khaganate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)

outcome.value: The Second Turkic Khaganate (682–744) was overthrown by the Uyghur Khaganate.

sources.value: Chinese records, Byzantine envoys and the Orkhon inscriptions. Checked against Wikipedia (“First Turkic Khaganate”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Dates for the split vary between sources (581 or 603).

knownFor.label: Orkhon inscriptions
knownFor.note: Stone monuments with the oldest Turkic texts.

sources: Wikipedia: First Turkic Khaganate (infobox, checked 6 Nov 2026)
